problem: By 2020 ObjectNav (navigate to an instance of a named object category in an unseen environment) was being defined in inconsistent ways. Papers and platforms differed on what counts as success (distance, visibility, stopping), on agent embodiment (actions, turn angles, body size, collision sliding) and on environments and categories. As a result, reported numbers could not be compared.
motivation: The earlier consensus by Anderson et al. (2018) on PointGoal navigation evaluation (SPL, an explicit STOP action) led to broad convergence and to shared challenges. ObjectGoal navigation now needs the same kind of precise specification. The authors observe that seemingly low-level details strongly change experimental outcomes. For example, collision 'sliding' lets learned agents cut through walls, as shown in Kadian et al.
key_idea: A multi-institution working group (FAIR, AI2, Georgia Tech, Google, SFU) fixes ObjectNav's success criterion, SPL variant, embodiment and environment choices, and instantiates them in the Habitat 2020 and RoboTHOR 2020 CVPR challenges.
insight: Success should be defined as a conjunction of four conditions: Intentionality (the agent emits STOP), Validity (the location is navigable), Proximity (within about r=1m of the object surface or bounding box) and Visibility (at least 1 object pixel, or oracle-visibility). Precomputing 'valid viewpoints' then turns object success into a PointNav-like geodesic check. Oracle-visibility decouples path finding from object framing. The paper also sets out known flaws of SPL: all failures score 0; variance is p·(1−p)·(1/N)·ΣSPL_i² when stopping is stochastic; in-place turning is free, so an agent can take a 360° panorama at no cost; and scores cannot be compared across datasets with different path lengths. It argues any future replacement metric should also replace SPL for ObjectNav. There are no ablations; the embodiment choices (30° turns, sliding disabled, LoCoBot dimensions) are justified by the sim2real findings of Kadian et al.
method: Success criterion: STOP is emitted at a navigable location, within a Euclidean shell (recommended r=1m, may be tightened) around the object surface (approximated by an axis-aligned or oriented 3D bounding box), with the object visible (at least 1 pixel) or under oracle-visibility (the object could be framed by in-place rotation or camera pitch/yaw).

ObjectNav-SPL: SPL_i = S_i·l_i/max(p_i,l_i), where l_i is the shortest path to the closest goal-category instance (reaching a farther instance still succeeds but lowers SPL). Known SPL issues are documented: no partial credit, high variance, no turning penalty, no cross-dataset comparability.
Embodiment recommendation: discretized differential drive with discrete actions (no low-level torque control); realistic synchronized sensors (RGB, depth, noisy egomotion or GPS+Compass).

Environment recommendation: photo-realistic scans of real spaces (MP3D; Gibson's 35 semantically labeled homes with a 25/5/5 split and suggested goals bed/chair/microwave/refrigerator/table/toilet/oven/tv/sofa; AI2-THOR iTHOR/RoboTHOR), a closed set of object classes, and train and test scenes from the same building distribution.

Habitat 2020 instantiation: 90 MP3D scenes on standard splits and 21 goal categories (training split: 8,349 instances in 71 environments). Valid viewpoints are sampled on an R_agent/2 grid within 1m of the object's oriented bounding box and must be visible under oracle-visibility. Episodes are limited to a shortest action path of at most 750 steps and a geodesic/Euclidean ratio of at least 1.05. The agent matches LoCoBot (radius 0.18m, height 0.88m), with actions forward 0.25m, turn L/R 30° (up from 10°), look up/down 30° and STOP. Sensors are an RGB-D camera (79° HFOV, 480×640, depth 0.5–6m) and noise-free GPS+Compass; collision sliding is disabled. Success means STOP within 0.1m geodesic of a valid viewpoint. Phases are minival, test-standard and test-challenge on EvalAI.

RoboTHOR 2020 instantiation: 89 scenes (75 simulated training scenes, split 60 train / 15 val; 4 test-dev scenes in sim and real; 10 real test-challenge scenes) with no overlap in wall layouts. There are 12 target categories out of 43, and object instances do not overlap across splits. The agent is a modified LoCoBot (0.88m tall, Azure Kinect camera with 79° FOV) with the same action set, evaluated in RGB-only and RGB-D tracks. Success means the target is within 1m and in the field of view; in the real world this is measured with Super-NIA-3D localization modules plus a manual visibility check.

setting.backbone: none (task-definition / benchmark specification paper; no agent proposed or evaluated)
setting.training_data: none (no model trained). Provides ObjectNav episode datasets: Habitat/MP3D '2 803K' episodes as printed in Table 1; RoboTHOR 34K episodes (easy/medium/hard by geodesic distance).
setting.observation: Habitat: egocentric RGB-D (79° HFOV, 480×640, depth clipped 0.5–6m) + idealized GPS+Compass. RoboTHOR: RGB-only or RGB-D at evaluation (localization and orientation sensors available in training).
setting.action_space: discrete: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, LOOK_UP/DOWN 30°, STOP (no sliding on collision)
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (Matterport3D); RoboTHOR/AI2-THOR (simulated scenes with physical twin scenes; physical LoCoBot evaluation specified for challenge phases 2–3 but no results reported here)
setting.privileged: none for the agent (GPS+Compass is noise-free in Habitat). Evaluation uses precomputed valid viewpoints under oracle-visibility.

numbers_note: No experimental or agent results are reported: this is a task-definition and challenge-specification paper. It contains only dataset statistics: Table 1 (Habitat: 90 scenes, 21 categories, ~397 instances per category, 4 per scene per category, geodesic 1/30 m, '2 803K' episodes; RoboTHOR: 89 scenes, 12 categories, ~20 instances per category, 1 per scene per category, 0.71/16.8 m, 34K episodes), plus distance distributions in Fig. 3 and Fig. 6. It states that test results would be published at the CVPR 2020 Embodied AI workshop.
results: There are no quantitative agent results. The contribution is a consensus ObjectNav specification. Success is defined as STOP near a navigable, object-visible viewpoint within 1m of the object, and SPL is measured to the closest instance. This is instantiated as the Habitat 2020 ObjectNav benchmark (MP3D, 21 categories, 0.1m-geodesic-to-viewpoint success, LoCoBot-matched RGB-D + GPS+Compass agent, no sliding) and the RoboTHOR 2020 sim-to-real benchmark (12 categories, 89 scenes, final test on 10 real scenes). Both became the standard HM3D/MP3D-ObjNav and RoboTHOR-ObjNav protocols used by later work.
limitations: SPL's known flaws (no partial credit, high variance, no turning penalty, no cross-dataset comparability) are acknowledged but not fixed; no new metric is proposed.

The Habitat setting uses idealized noise-free sensors and discrete actions without robot dynamics, and success uses a lenient oracle-visibility criterion. Real-world transfer is only covered by the RoboTHOR track.
Closed-set object categories only, indoor only; no baseline results are provided in the paper.
builds_on: On Evaluation of Embodied Navigation Agents (Anderson et al. 2018)
